course.description: Build a reusable Cowork task that scans a client folder, populates your workpaper templates (income, deductions, CGT, loans), and flags review items by priority — turning hours of manual prep into minutes.
learningOutcomes: Apply the methods taught in Set Up the Workpaper Populator Skill in Claude Cowork.

lessons.content:
The **Workpaper Populator** skill is a saved Cowork task that scans a client's document folder and populates your workpaper templates — flagging anything that needs review before you touch it.

**What it handles:**
- Scans uploaded client documents (bank statements, payslips, receipts, loan docs, etc.)
- Maps data into your workpaper templates: income, deductions, CGT events, loan schedules
- Flags review items by priority — high (errors/missing), medium (needs verification), low (informational)
- Outputs populated templates ready for your review and sign-off

**Why build it as a skill:** Client engagements follow the same structure — set it up once and run it at the start of every client file.
lessons.title: What this skill does

lessons.content:
1. Open **Claude Cowork** on your desktop
2. Click **New Task**
3. Name it: **Workpaper Populator**
4. Leave the task open — the next step is where you write the instructions that make this a real skill

> **Note:** In Cowork, a "skill" is simply a task with good instructions. The name you give it is what you'll see every time you open it. Keep it short and descriptive — "Workpaper Populator" is perfect.
lessons.title: Create the task in Cowork

activities.title: Write the skill instructions (this is the skill)

lessons.content:
In the task instructions field, paste the prompt below. **Replace the template fields and section names with your firm's actual workpaper structure.**

---

*"You are my Workpaper Populator. Each time I run this task, I will upload a client's source documents for the current engagement.*

*Review all uploaded documents and populate the following workpaper sections — replace these with your actual templates:*

- *Income section: Extract all income sources — salary (from payslips/group certificates), interest (bank statements), dividends (dividend statements), rental income (lease agreements/statements) → Add or remove income types relevant to your engagements*
- *Deductions section: Identify deductible expenses — work-related (receipts, invoices), vehicle (logbook or cents-per-km), home office → Replace with your firm's standard deduction categories*
- *CGT section: Identify any asset disposals — shares, property, other. Extract acquisition date, cost base, sale date, proceeds → Note if CGT events appear in the documents*
- *Loans section: Extract loan balances, interest charges, and lender details from any loan statements provided*

*For each section, flag review items by priority:*
- *HIGH: Missing required documents, inconsistencies, or figures that need verification before lodgement*
- *MEDIUM: Items present but require professional judgement or client confirmation*
- *LOW: Informational notes only*

*Output each section as a separate table, followed by a consolidated priority flag list."*

---

> **Make it yours:** Add your firm's workpaper section names exactly as they appear in your templates. Include any jurisdiction-specific rules (e.g. ATO thresholds, specific CGT concessions).
lessons.title: Write the skill instructions (this is the skill)

activities.title: Run it and save your skill

lessons.content:
Your skill is ready. Here's how to use it the first time and every time after.

**First run:**
1. Open the **Workpaper Populator** task you just set up
2. Upload a sample client's documents — use a straightforward engagement for the first test
3. Review the populated sections and priority flags
4. Check that the section names match your actual workpaper templates
5. Refine the instructions if sections are missing or flags aren't categorised correctly

**Every engagement after that:**
1. Open the **Workpaper Populator** task
2. Upload the new client's documents
3. Review the populated output and HIGH priority flags first
4. Transfer the data into your formal workpaper templates and address flagged items before lodgement

**Tips:**
- Run it at the start of every client file — it front-loads the data entry so you spend your time reviewing, not keying
- HIGH priority flags are your review list — work through them before signing off
- If a client type has different document requirements (e.g. sole trader vs. individual), create a separate task variant for each

You now have a Workpaper Populator skill that turns hours of document prep into a first-pass review in minutes.
